text: Progen A is a Holofigure in . It depicts a white and golden progen variant. It can be obtained from Celestin, the Spring Storm in Primordia.
Progen B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a brown and silver progen variant. It can be obtained from Ernest, the Contemplative in Oblivia.
Progen C is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a green and blue progen variant. It can be obtained from Blaudolch, the Chalcedony in Sylvalum.
Potamus A is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a black potamus variant. It can be obtained from Mesgen, the Fairweathered in Primordia.
Potamus B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a brown potamus variant. It can be obtained from Rodriguez, the Twin-Tusked in Cauldros.

Pride Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Factory 1.21 Longsword. It is obtained as a reward for completing either the Normal Mission Fortun and Glory or Definian Love. The Pride weapons available in-game are: * Archetype Pride * Iron Pride * Carbide Pride * Cermet Pride * Chrome Pride * Chromoly Pride * Cobalt Pride * Titanium Pride * Ceramic Pride * Diamond Pride

Potamus Peril is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.8, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting twenty-four Forfexes. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Preventing Vengeance is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.17, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting five Jia Mian, the Beloveds. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.
Potential Drive is a ground armor Skell Augment in and that increases the potential of the party member's Skell. Its effect caps at 100%.
PositionDmg.FRONT is a Skell frame attack augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell damage by 10% to 50% when attacking from the front. The ground equivalent is Front Attack Plus.
PositionDMG.SIDE is a Skell frame attack augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell damage by 10% to 50% when attacking from the side. The ground equivalent is Side Attack Plus.
PositionDmg.BACK is a Skell frame attack augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell damage by 10% to 50% when attacking from behind. The ground equivalent is Back Attack Plus.
PositionDmg.ABOVE is a Skell frame attack augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It increases Skell damage by 10% to 50% when attacking from above. The ground equivalent is Vantage Attack Plus.

Prime Diving Band Rs are Casual Wear right arm armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.

Prime Hoodies are Casual Wear upper-body armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.
Prime Jackets are Casual Wear upper-body armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.
Prime Tees are Casual Wear upper-body armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.
Prime Workwear are Casual Wear upper body armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries.

Prime Sport Glasses are Casual Wear head armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries. They are an upgraded version of the Sport Glasses and share their appearance with them.
Prime Swimmer's Band Ls are Casual Wear left arm armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries and are a part of the Swimmer armor range.
Prime Swimmer's Band Rs are Casual Wear right arm armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Sakuraba Industries and are a part of the Swimmer armor range.

Pouches (Japanese: , Pōchi) are a mechanic in and . They are inventory elements carried by each character where consumable items, known as Pouch items (, Pōchiaitemu), are stored and conserved. These various items fall into specific categories. When an item is put into a Pouch, it lasts for a certain amount of time, during which it grants one or more benefits to the user. It also slightly increases the Trust of all Blades engaged to that Driver. The timer for a Pouch item runs in real time and pauses when using menus. After it runs out, if another item of the same name exists in the inventory it will automatically refill the Pouch and extend its effects. Otherwise, the Pouch will become empt

The Praetor's Study (Japanese: , Hō'ō Shitsumushitsu) is a location in . It is located in the Indoline Sanctum in the Indoline Praetorium. As its name implies, it is where Praetor Amalthus spends much of his time cleansing Core Crystals. The summit of world leaders also takes place here after the incident on Temperantia.

Precious Yearnings (Japanese: , Menou no Ishi, Agate's Will) is a Blade Quest in . It can be received from Agate by resting at the Folmarie Inn in the Commercial District of Fonsa Myma, Uraya while Agate, Pyra, Nia, Tora, Mòrag, and Zeke are in the party. This quest is required to advance Agate's "Prospecting" Skill and to unlock her Key Affinity Reward levels 3 – 5.
The Port-side Walkway (Japanese: , Sagen Gaikaku Tsūro) is a landmark in . It is located on the Titan Battleship in the Gormott Province, between the Cloud Tank Chamber and Solitary Block #1.

Port Anangham (Japanese: , Anan'yamu-kō) is a Location in . It is located on the Lower Level of the Empire of Mor Ardain. It is the primary port facility for the Titan's left shoulder, and is not far from the Empire's capital Alba Cavanich. It is the first location on the Mor Ardain Titan the party visits upon their arrival.

The Portal of the Hero (Japanese: , Eiyū no Mon) is a landmark in . It is located on the Lower Level of Spirit Crucible Elpys, beween the Chamber of Pillars and the Vault of Heroes. There are no enemies here, but there is a Salvage Point and hidden Treasure Trove.
Pomegranate Soups are Veggie Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Sadecott Groceries in Garfont Village in the Kingdom of Uraya.
Prickly Snowpickles are Veggie Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Lectica Vegetables in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal. They are one of Vale's favorite Pouch items.
The Praximo Deeds are a Store Deed key item in . They can be purchased from Praximo Cosmetics in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal.
Prideful Walking are Literature Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Biblio Paulio in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal.
Portraits of Ger the Hero are Art Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Memoria Art in Theosoir in the Kingdom of Tantal. They are one of the favorite Pouch items of Zenobia.
Pow-Pow Cannon (Japanese: , Dokodoko Kyanon) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Tora's arts when using Mech Arms.
Praximo Cosmetics is a shop in . It is run by Dyphne and can be found in the Kingdom of Tantal's Theosoir. It is specialized in Cosmetics.

The Profaned Place (Japanese: , Bōtoku no Chi) is a Secret Area in . It is located on the Central Plain of Temperantia, at the end of a small, valley-like path directly west of the Ardainian Garrison. The Superboss Tyrannotitan Kurodil can be found here, as well as seven Ignas. The 7 Ignas consist of 3 Bagis Ignas, 3 Mergen Ignas, and 1 Amost Igna. Three Treasure Troves also reside here, behind the Ignas. The wooden Treasure Trove requires Level 3 Lockpicking, and Level 2 Ancient Wisdom. The red Treasure Trove requires Level 4 Lockpicking, and Level 3 Ancient Wisdom. The white Treasure Trove requires Level 5 Lockpicking, and Level 5 Ancient Wisdom.

Praetorian Medea (Japanese: , Hōō Chokuzoku no Meigasu) is a Unique Monster in . It is an Indoline Sentinel-type Titan that can be found at level 66 at the far end of the 7th Perimeter Skyport on the World Tree. It must be defeated to unlock Dromarch's level 5 Raging Tiger Special as well as Zenobia's level 5 "The Indomitable" Battle Skill.

Prom Piranhax (Japanese: , Puromu Samon) are enemies in . They are members of the Piranhax family and can be found at level 19-22 on the Upper Level - Right of the Gormott Province when it is raining, or anytime except Night Incense at Eight-Rock Skip in the Stomach of the Kingdom of Uraya after climbing towards the waterfall. Five of them must be defeated to unlock Perun's level 2 "Silent Spear" and Dagas' level 2 Tyrant Crush, and four to unlock T-elos's level 2 "Phase Transition Tech".
Poppi's Remodel? is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located in Tora's House in the Gormott Province.
Prismatic Headbands are Textile Pouch items in . They can be purchased at Future Crafts in Fonsett Village in the Leftherian Archipelago.

Pride Drivers (Japanese: , Puraido Doraibā) are enemies in . They are Driver enemies, and can be found at level 95 at the Olethro Playhouse in the Kingdom of Uraya, where they assist the Unique Monster Beast-Hunter William.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Priestess's Auspices (Japanese: , Miko no Gofu) are accessories in and . They boost the wearer's resistance to the Shackle Driver debuff by up to 70%. The Sage's Auspices accessory offers a stronger instance of this equipment's effect.
Pound Vipers are Insect collectibles in . They can be found in the Land of Morytha.
Prism Tubes are Mechanical collectibles in . They can be found in the Leftherian Archipelago.

|-|Common = |-|Rare = |-|Legendary = Promise Rings are accessories in and . They increase the HP restored when reviving a teammate by up to 39% of their maximum health. They are the upgraded version of the Friendship Ring and Affection Ring accessories. This equipment can stack with the additive HP recovering effects of the teammate's Grandarbor Ward, Spirit Tree Ward or World Tree Ward accessories.

Premium Cylinders are cylinders in . They are the best cylinders available. They can reliably yield gold and white treasure chests, which have the highest chance of containing rare Treasure Items. Premium cylinders can randomly appear in shops on Titans which have reached a certain Development Level for 25,000 G. A small number of them can be received from Mochichi as rewards for increasing Rex's Salvager Rank. With the New Quests Pack 1 DLC installed, Premium Cylinders can be crafted by Budada in Goldmouth Res. Dist. after completing the quest M.I.A. Nopon in which he must be rescued. To craft one Premium Cylinder, four Golden Cylinders, two Silver Cylinders and one Chain of Keys (which can
Preserved Dwarves are Treasure items in . They can be obtained by Salvaging at Port Anangham in the Empire of Mor Ardain.
Precipitous Impact (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Zeke's arts when using a Bitball. In the , it is also one of Zeke's arts when using Bunnie.

Pouch Expansion Kits are Key Items in and . Each can be used to permanently allow a Driver to have two Pouch items in effect at the same time. There are six of them in total around Alrest, so each character can have the extra pouch.

Polygon Chips are Core Chips in and . They can be obtained as rewards from three quests, one of which (Beneath the Aurora) is DLC only, and dropped by two enemies in the Cliffs of Morytha. In they can only be dropped by Ionospheric Mitchell. Polygon Chips share their appearance with Cube Chips, Sphere Chips, and Spiral Chips. __TOC__
Positron Chips are Core Chips in . They can be dropped by a variety of enemies. Positron Chips share their appearance with Hadron Chips and Photon Chips. __TOC__

Preon Chips are Core Chips in . They can be dropped by Chickenheart Dagmara. They possess the highest auto-attack value in the game. Preon Chips share their appearance with Dilaton Chips and Tachyon Chips (with the exception of for Rare Blades). __TOC__
Praxis's Core Crystal is a special Core Crystal in . It allows the party to awake Praxis and can be obtained as a reward after completing Crystal Clear.

Prink Medoozes (Japanese: , Purinku Jerī) are enemies in . They are members of the Medooz family, and can be found at level 51-55 when salvaging at the Canyon of Husks or Portal of the Hero in the Spirit Crucible Elpys.

Promotional Leaflets are three Key Items in . They are obtained from Falala at the Rumbletum Canteen in the Argentum Trade Guild after delivering the required ingredients during the quest Fame and Family.
The Production Admin Office (Japanese: , Seizō Jimukyoku) is a Landmark in . It is located in the Old Factory of the Empire of Mor Ardain.
Prevarr Trading is a shop in . It can be found at Goetuis Port in the Indoline Praetorium. It is run by Rynello and is specialized in Exchange.
Poyopoyo is an NPC in . He is a Nopon who can be found at Kloom Farm in the Gormott Province, and gives information for the quest Crane Criminals.
The Port Deck (Japanese: , Sagen Kanpan) is a Location in . It is located on the Titan Battleship in the Gormott Province, accessed from the Bridge.

The Port Balcony (Japanese: , Sagen Kōbu Dekki) is a location in . It is located on the Titan Battleship in the Gormott Province. There are no enemies here. Finch's Heart-to-Heart, "Bird's-Eye View", is located here.

The Profiteering Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission Shipyard Security. It enables the purchase of How Wars Profit Nopon from the Haskefell Books shop at Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain.

The Prismatic Contract is a Key Item in . It is received as a reward after completing the Merc Mission Ship Lane Lighting. It enables the purchase of Prismatic Headbands from the Future Crafts shop at Fonsett Village in the Leftherian Archipelago.
Porcupine Blow is a Driver Art in . It is one of Nia's arts when using a Decimation Cannon.

Popono is an NPC in . He is a Nopon found on a wooden balcony in Torika Alley of Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya. He offers the Merc Mission Fort Rescue. Popono is a bit difficult to reach, as he requires a few Field Skills and a trip around the alley to get to him. He claims to be a spy scouting for the Urayan military and brags about his intelligence and info gathering skills.

Profligate Sjell (Japanese: , Hōtō no Shanku) is a quest-exclusive enemy in . He is a Driver enemy who can be found at level 58 at the Balquors Ruins in the Cliffs of Morytha alongside Meddlesome Zacharias during the DLC Quest Upgrades and Tinkering. Although it is not specifically required to defeat these enemies to complete the quest, they serve as obstacles to one of its objectives and must be fought or otherwise evaded to continue onwards. Upon completing said objective, both enemies will permanently despawn.

Popoh is an NPC in . She is a Nopon who can be found on a cliff above the Garfont Training Ground in the Kingdom of Uraya, if hired. She is one of three NPCs who can be hired as admin of the Garfont Mercenaries during the quest Leadership Qualities.

Presser Lizards (Japanese: , Puressā Rizado) are Story Exclusive Enemies in . They are members of the Lizard family, and can be found at level 27 - 29 in the Old Factory of the Empire of Mor Ardain during Chapter 4.
The Posystone is a Key Item in . It is obtained inside Pippito's Haunt in the Kingdom of Tantal during the DLC Quest Beneath the Aurora.

Pro Swimmer Pyra (Japanese: ) is a DLC Aux Core in . It reduces the damage taken from field hazards such as poisoned pools of water and fire by 35%. It also changes Pyra's appearance when she equips the core, granting her a one piece black swimsuit. It can be purchased at the DLC shop Noponstone Exchange for 45 Flawless Noponstones in the Land of Challenge obtained after completing a Challenge Battle, available as downloadable content from the Challenge Battle Mode Pack of the Expansion Pass. The DLC Aux Cores Beach Date Pandoria, Radiant Beach Mythra and Water Lily Brighid have the same effect. The Skill RAM/Upgrade variant Swim Lesson Poppi α grants Poppi α, Poppi QT and Poppi QTπ an equiv
The Pouch Item Emporium is a DLC Shop in . It is run by the Archsage's Private Chef and can be found in the Land of Challenge after collecting the Nopon Invitation, Pt. 2 on Version 1.5.2 or later.
Profundity Grace (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Zeke's arts when wielding Dual Swords.

Preoccupied Gogols (Japanese: , Okupādo Gogōru) are Story and Quest Exclusive Enemies in . They are members of the Gogol family and can be found at level 24 in the Aletta Region of the Kingdom of Torna, on Wrackham Moor. Two of them must be defeated during Lett Bridge Restoration. As with all Quest-exclusive Enemies in , Preoccupied Gogols drop no items, only gold.
Preparing for the Worst are Script items in . They can be created by Minoth at Campsites.
Prime Glasses are Casual Wear head armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Grenada Galactic Group.

Prime Sunglasses are Casual Wear head armor in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are manufactured by Grenada Galactic Group. They are an upgraded version of the Sunglasses and share their appearance with them.

Prologue: Awakening is introduced after the opening cutscene, character creation, and [https://xenoblade.fandom.com/wiki/Cross Cross]'s first interaction with [https://xenoblade.fandom.com/wiki/Elma Elma] in [https://xenoblade.fandom.com/wiki/Xenoblade%20Chronicles%20X Xenoblade Chronicles X]. It consists of Elma and Cross's journey through southwest Primordia to [https://xenoblade.fandom.com/wiki/New%20Los%20Angeles New Los Angeles] after Elma rescues Cross from a crashed lifepod in Starfall Basin. [https://xenoblade.fandom.com/wiki/Chapter%201 Chapter 1] automatically begins after the Prologue is completed. The Prologue includes gameplay tutorials to familiarize the player with a few basic

Popolo is an NPC in . He is a Nopon who can be found at the Formide Shopping Ward of Auresco in the Kingdom of Torna, where he works as Morumo's aide. Popolo gives no quests himself, but his Community is gained alongside Macmac and Morumo's upon completion of A Rare Sense of Justice.

Prado Caterpiles (Japanese: , Purado Kyapiru) are quest exclusive enemies in . They are members of the Caterpile family, and can be found at level 39 in the Kingdom of Torna during the quest Homegrown Inventor. As with all quest exclusive enemies in , they drop no items, only gold.

The Ponspectors (Japanese: , Noponjā, Nopongers) are a brigade of twelve Nopon in . They are an elite band of surveyors from Frontier Village's Archaeology Centre, split between red, blue and yellow teams. The Ponspectors are NPCs that the party can find and meet all over Bionis' Shoulder, and they can be recruited. They have issues they struggle with and give the party a quest in order to gain each Ponspector's aid in battle. Once recruited and assembled, they can provide Union Strikes and extra effects during battles. It should be noted that certain Ponspectors, when recruited, may offer hints on the location of their companions. These are shown as a Ponspector flag on the map.

Pororo is a Nopon in . She can initially be found on a plateau beyond Skybridge on the Bionis' Shoulder. She has lost her favourite foodstuffs all over the Bionis' Shoulder and gives the quest Lost & Found in request that the party recover them for her. After completion of her quest, she moves to Gran Dell. She traveled to the Bionis' Shoulder with Bana, whom she refers to as her "esteemed person".
Pororo's Favourites are Key Items in . There are twenty in total found across the Bionis' Shoulder. They are required to be given to Pororo during Lost & Found.
Princess Dresses D are Unique light torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. They can only be worn by Melia.

Praying Caterpile Control (Japanese: , Pureā Kyapiru wo Tōbatsuseyo) is a quest in . It can be received once Laennar's Worries from Laennar is accepted at Companions' Cape on Bionis' Shoulder, or later at Agni's Birthplace.
Ponspectors Till We Cry (Japanese: , Noponjā Egao no Saishūkai) is a quest in . It can be received from Wunwun at Gran Dell Approach on the Bionis' Shoulder. It is the final Ponspector quest.

Priority Wunwun (Japanese: , Taichō Wanawana no Shirei) is a quest in . It can be received from Wunwun at the Gran Dell Approach on the Bionis' Shoulder. Completing it unlocks Ponspectors Till We Cry.
Prodigal Gauntlets are medium arms armour in and . They can be bought at shops for 480 G.
Prodigal Girdles are medium legs armour in and . They can be bought at shops for 480 G.
Prodigal Helms are medium head armour in and . They can be bought at shops for 600 G.
Prodigal Greaves are medium feet armour in and . They can be bought at shops for 720 G.
Prodigal Cuirasses are medium torso armour in and . They can be bought at shops for 1,200 G.
Princess Bottoms are light legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. They are the initial starting equipment for Melia, and can only be worn by her.
Princess Bottoms D are light legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. They can only be worn by Melia.
Princess Bottoms L are light legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. They can only be worn by Melia.
Princess Dresses are light torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. They are the initial starting equipment for Melia, and can only be worn by her.
Princess Dresses L are light torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles: Future Connected. They can only be worn by Melia.

Prominence Revolt (Japanese: ) is Pyra's Level II Blade Special in .
Poppi Ignition (Japanese: , Hana igunishon, Lit. "Hana Ignition") is Poppi QTπ's Level I Blade Special in .
Poppi Unlimited (Japanese: , Hana anrimiteddo, Lit. "Hana Unlimited") is Poppi QTπ's Level III Blade Special in . Poppi Unlimited is also Poppi QTπ's Special Art during Merc Assault missions in the .
Poppi Spinning Slash (Japanese: , Hana Supinkattā, Lit. "Hana Spin Cutter") is Poppi α's Level I Blade Special in .
Poppi Drill (Japanese: , Hana doriru, Lit. "Hana Drill") is Poppi α's Level III Blade Special in . Poppi Drill is also Poppi α's Special Art during Merc Assault missions in the .
Poppi Missile (Japanese: , Hana misairu, Lit. "Hana Missile") is Poppi QT's Level I Blade Special in .
Poppi Crushing Blow (Japanese: , Hana kurasshā, Lit. "Hana Crusher") is Poppi QT's Level II Blade Special in .
Prism Pickaxe is a Key Item in . It can be crafted by Hugo at Campsites.
Pressure Drop (Japanese: , Puresshādoroppu) is a Talent Art in . It is the Talent Art of the Ogre class. It deals considerable damage while being an early source of the Launch effect.
Preparing for Battle is a Standard Quest in . It can be received in Colony 9 in Yzana Plains.
The Precipice of Judgment (Japanese: , Sabaki no Zeppeki) is a Location in , located on Ribbi Flats in the Fornis Region.

Prayer Necklaces are Accessories in and . They can be purchased at the Colony 9 Commissary, and they are one of the items that can be used to complete the mission Korresia Finds Her Calling. In , they can be dropped by normal enemies level 9 to 16.

Predator's Paw (Japanese: , Majū no Tenohira) is a Landmark in . It is located in Erythia Sea, to the east of Anu Shoals. It is the remains of one of the Hovering Reefs from Eryth Sea. There is a large monument located here that releases the Depriti Pippito during Unspeakable Being.
The Prison Camp, Freight Gate (Japanese: , Gaikaku Kaihōguchi) is a Landmark in . It is located at the Agnus Castle Barbican. It serves as the main entrance into Li Garte Prison Camp.
The Prison Precipice (Japanese: , Kyokuten no Sandō) is a Location in . It is located behind the Agnus Castle Barbican in the Cadensia Region. It leads to the Vent Entrance of Li Garte Prison Camp.

Profound Hodzuki (Japanese: , Gaihaki no Hoodzuki) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Quadwing family, and can be found at level 44 at Visura Parkland on Elaice Highway. The Hypnotism Art can be earned for the Soulhacker class by defeating it.

Pressing Rafeel (Japanese: , Semarikuru Radorieru) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Enpedia family, and can be found at level 69 in the Hangar, Lower Level in the Origin Interior. The Defense Mastery Skill can be earned for the Soulhacker class by defeating it.
Promise to the Future (Japanese: , Mirai e no Chikai) is an Ascension Quest in , dedicated to Monica.
Potatwoes are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Fornis Region. They can also be purchased from the Colony Iota Caravan, or produced from the Desert Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Project-a-Blade are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Pentelas Region. They can also be produced from the Cascade Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Preserved Gogol Snacks are Collectible items in and . They can be dropped by Gogol enemies.

|-|XC3 = |-|FR = Powder Pearls are Gemstone Collectible items in and . They can be found in the Pentelas Region in . They can also be produced from the Clifftop Ferronis Hulk Fabricator. They can be found on the Aurora Shelf in .
Prickle Spices are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Aetia Region. It can also be purchased from the Colony 9 Caravan, or produced from the Hillside Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Popper Pumpkins are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Aetia Region. They can also be produced from the Hillside Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Ponio Fossils are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Aetia Region. They can also be produced from the Hillside Ferronis Hulk Fabricator. They are fossilized Ponios.
Powdered Wheats are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Fornis Region. They can also be purchased from the Colony 30 Caravan, or produced from the Tableland Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.
Prom Fliers are Normal Enemies in . They are members of the Flier family, and can be found at level 16-18 in Ribbi Flats.
Polychromiums are Collectible items in . They can be found in the Cadensia Region. They can also be produced from the Atoll Ferronis Hulk Fabricator.

Poseidon Merignas are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Merigna family, and can be found at level 45 at the Sea Lizards' Tide Pool and level 97-98 at the Emerald Font in Erythia Sea. They ride on Merfreys.
The Prison Warden (Japanese: , Kanbōchō) is an NPC in . He is the warden of Li Garte Prison Camp.
Princess Brogs are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Brog family, and can be found at level 22-23 at Yzana Plains and Millick Meadows in the Aetia Region.

Prithee Pippitos are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Pippito family, and can be found at level 12-13 in Millick Meadows. Two are also fought at level 52 during the final wave of the Challenge Battle Pretty Fierce.

Pon-Fried Croquettes are Meal items in . They can be purchased from the Colony Mu Canteen. They are unlocked after completing the Quest: Crusader For Spuds, and choosing Colony Mu. Doing so locks you out of the meal item from Colony 4: Ta-da-to Surprise.

Princess Arachno (Japanese: , Purinsesu Supaido) is a Quest Exclusive Boss in . It is a member of the Arachno family, and is fought at level 26 in the Urayan Tunnels during A Nopon's Counsel alongside 5 Savant Arachnos.
Prize X-change Red is a DLC Shop in . It is run by the Archsage's Page, Red and can be found in the Land of Challenge, available as part of the Challenge Battle Mode of the Expansion Pass.

Pretty Fierce is a Time Attack Challenge Battle in . It can be received from Nopon Archsage in the Land of Challenge, available as downloadable content from the second part of the Expansion Pass. Clearing this challenge with at least an A rank for the first time will unlock the Swimwear B outfit for Mio.

Primate Triumvirate is a Time Attack Challenge Battle in . It can be received from Nopon Archsage in the Land of Challenge, available as downloadable content from the second part of the Expansion Pass. Clearing this challenge with at least an A rank for the first time will reward the player with an Accomplished Crown.

Predation (Japanese: , Lit. "Gluttony") is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Soulhacker class. It is acquired by defeating the Unique Monster Ruthless Grokken while the Soul Hack skill is set on any player-controlled party member.
Pride of Place is a Talent Art in . It is the Talent Art of the Lapidarist class.
Prismatic Ring is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Lapidarist class.

Prize X-change Blue is a DLC Shop in . It is run by the Archsage's Page, Blue and can be found in the Land of Challenge, available as part of the Challenge Battle Mode of the Expansion Pass. This shop becomes available after the player's first run through the Archsage's Gauntlet. Blue Noponstone is traded for items here.
Predator Masks are DLC Accessories in . They can be purchased from Prize X-change Blue in the Land of Challenge for 6000 Noponstones.
Prime Round Sunglasses are Casual Wear head armor in . They are manufactured by Grenada Galactic Group and are apart of the Custom Diving armor range.
Private Ignas are two Quest Exclusive Bosses in . They are members of the Igna family that are fought at level 52 in Zalmor's Thawtunnels on the Aurora Shelf during Takedown: Ignas.
Prohibitor Giuseppe (Japanese: , Heisoku no Geroruto) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Brog family, and can be found at level 23 in the Inconspicuous Cave of Vermilion Woods.

Praetor Amalthus - The Acting God - is a track from , composed by Yasunori Mitsuda. It is track five of disc five on the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track five of disc ten on the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. It is a remix of Past From Far Distance. This song plays during the battle against Amalthus. This track also appears as a DLC music track in , included alongside Pyra and Mythra's Fighter Pack. It is a track option on Gaur Plain, the Cloud Sea of Alrest, Final Destination, and the three variants of Battlefield.

The Pretty Core Crystal is a special Core Crystal in . It allows the party to awaken MOMO. It is given to the party by Tora in his house in Torigoth after he and Poppi join the party. Receiving the Pretty Core Crystal also activates the quest Tora's Secret Stash.
Potential is a stat in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It affects the amount of damage dealt by TP Arts as well as the amount of HP recovered by Battle Arts and Soul Voices.
Potential Down is a debuff in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It decreases the amount of HP recovered by Soul Voices and Arts and the damage dealt by Tension Arts.

Quests are a collection of requests in that the many people of Bionis and Mechonis ask of the party, or that are automatically triggered in the course of the story. Most quests do not need to be completed to advance the story, but some do. There are also Timed Quests, which must be completed before a certain point in the story, such as the refugees moving back to Colony 6 or before the destruction of Galahad Fortress. There are also some Mutually Exclusive Quests, where the party must choose one option or the other; depending on the choice, the Affinity Chart will grow differently. There are also some Story Quests and a few Surprise Quests that will appear during the progression of the story

Puko (Japanese: ) is a Nopon in . He can be found at the back side of the weapon shop at Kyn Shopping Street in Frontier Village. He is the medicine supplier for Medi who has had the medicine made by the High Entia attacked multiple times by the Abominable Hiln and has to make his own medicine to compensate for it.

Puera Telethia (Japanese: , Puera Tereshia) are a group of three Bosses in . They are Phoenix-type members of the Telethia family, and are fought by Shulk and Alvis at level 28 at the Lakeside in Makna Forest. They are the spawn of the much more formidable Leone Telethia.

Quadwing Bags (Japanese: , Kurōdo no Takarabukuro) are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are dropped by Coppice Quadwings lying on the trees of the Satorl Marsh during the day. A good number of these birds can be seen around Barren Moor. According to their description, they are bags perfect for holding valuables and they preserve the quality of their contents. Two are needed for Colony 6 Reconstruction. In Definitive Edition, they can be purchased in Time Attack place from Nopon Archsage for 1,200 Noponstones.

Rabbit Diodes (Japanese: , Rabitto Daiōdo) are collectables in . They can be found in Colony 9. According to their description, they are cute pink machine parts reminiscent of a bunny's tail. Three are required for Colony 6 Reconstruction, and two more are required for Collection Quest 1 in Colony 9. In , they can be purchased from the Nopon Archsage in Time Attack for 3,000 Noponstones.
Qofaria (Japanese: , Yūforia, Euphoria) is a Machina in . She is the mother of Mixik and the wife of Kazat. She can be found near the pipe surrounding the Hidden Machina Village on the Fallen Arm.
Pyro Lizards (Japanese: , Bomumakitokage) are collectables in . They can be found in Colony 6. According to their description, they are covered in bumpy skin and they turn fiery red when disturbed.

Purple Lamps (Japanese: , Pāpuru Raito) are collectables in . They can be found in Sword Valley and Colony 6. According to their description, they are lamps that emit a purple light and their glow is profoundly mysterious.

Proof of Status (Japanese: , Nopon Shōkai no Akashi) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Daza in the Watchpoint Junction in the outskirts of Colony 6, or at the Hope Farm Shop once the Reconstruction started. After completing this quest, Safety First will become available. If Shulk is in the active party, he will comment.

Queen Locusts (Japanese: , Yuuhibatta) are collectables in . They can be found on Bionis' Leg. According to their description, they are deep red like the setting sun and they are popular gifts for ladies.

Pure Cherries (Japanese: , Pyua Aserora, Pure Acerola) are collectables in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found in Makna Forest. According to their description, they usually grow beside clean water and eating them brings clarity. Two are required for Collection Quest 2 in Frontier Village.
Rag Bone Hammers (Japanese: , Ragubōnhanmā) are weapons in . They are gunlances wielded by Reyn.

Ragrinar Canyon Path (Japanese: , Ragurina Keikoku-dо̄) is a landmark in . It is located on the lower level of Bionis' Leg. It is at the entrance to Bionis' Leg from Tephra Cave. On this path a shop and some unnamed Homs travelers can be found, who will give the party four Quests. There are no enemies here.
Prox (Japanese: , Purimo) is a Machina in . She can be found in the Hidden Machina Village on the Fallen Arm, kneeling at the water just north of the Ether Light at night.
Prototype Helms (Japanese: , Shisaku-gata Jūsō Herumu) are heavy head armour in . They can be bought at a shop in Colony 9. They are newly developed by the Colony 9 Defence Force.
Protector Amulets are light arms armour in . They can be traded for with Dionysis.
Quark Gear (Japanese: , Kuōku Gia) is medium head armour in . It is reinforced with quartz from Gaur Plain on Bionis' Leg. It can be dropped by Aqua Nebulae.
Quark Armour is medium torso armour in . It is made with quartz from Gaur Plain. It can be obtained as a quest reward after completing A Thoughtful Idea.

The Prophecy Hut (Japanese: , Otsuge no Ma) is a landmark in . It is located on the seventh floor of Frontier Village. It is a hut in the middle of the Mysterious Sanctuary level. It is where Chief Dunga has his prophecies. Inside the hut Miko can be found, who gives the party a quest requiring them to find Pelupelu. After that quest, Pelupelu will be found at the Prophecy Hut. A Heart-to-Heart - "A Mysterious Sanctuary" - is located here.
Quark Gauntlets are medium arms armour in . They can be obtained as a quest reward after completing Out-of-Luck Giorgio. They are made with quartz from Gaur Plain.
Quark Leggings are medium legs armour in . They are made with quartz from Gaur Plain. They can be obtained as a quest reward after completing Pestering Paola.
Rafaga Leggings are medium leg armour in and . They can be obtained as a quest reward after completing various quests, or be dropped by various enemies.
Quark Boots are medium feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are reinforced with quartz from Gaur Plain.
Queen Frogs (Japanese: , Kuīnfuroggu) are weapons in . They are biters that can be wielded by Riki.

The Radio Tower (Japanese: , Denpatō) is a landmark in . It is located in the south of Sword Valley. It overlooks Galahad Fortress from the side. When the party first reaches the Radio Tower, Secure the Radio Tower is triggered, where the party must defeat the Lightning Ronove, along with the other Mechon surrounding it.

Protect the Village (Japanese: , Sato no Buji wo Kakuhoshite) is a quest in . It can be received from Eleqa in front of the entrance of Hidden Machina Village on the Fallen Arm. If Dunban is in the active party, he will comment.

Prudent Purson (Japanese: , Shiryo no Puruson) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a Mechon, and can be found at level 49 at the Dolgan Outpost in Sword Valley. As part of a surprise quest, Secure Dolgan Outpost, it and two M63X Android Units must be defeated so Dolgan Outpost can be seized. There is also a M46 Covert Killer that is patrolling the hall by the room that will alert the Prudent Purson to the party's presence. When the party first arrives at Sword Valley in the story, they travel through the valley seizing all the miniature fortresses and outposts along the way while heading to the main fortress, Galahad Fortress.
Punish the Hodes (Japanese: , Fūdi wo Seibaiseyo) is a quest in . It is automatically received when Trouble at the Plant is accepted from Jarack at the Ether Plant in the Eryth Sea.
Quitters (Japanese: , Mikkabōzu) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are swords wielded by Dunban.
Purity Strikers (Japanese: , Junsei no Tachi, Pure Tachi) are weapons in . They are swords wielded by Dunban.
Queen Clusters (Japanese: , Kuīnkurasutā) are weapons in . They are rifles that can be wielded by Sharla.
Prosperity Biters (Japanese: , Han'ei no Kamukamu) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are biters wielded by Riki. They can be acquired by trading with Eiz who can be found on the Fallen Arm.
Protector Daggers (Japanese: , Purotekutodagā) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are Fiora's twin blades, and can be dropped by enemies in Mechonis Field.
The Protect Staff (Japanese: , Goshinjō, Self-Defence Staff) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is the weapon carried by Melia when she first joins the party.
Rafaga Gear (Japanese: , Rāfaga Gia) is medium head armour in and . They can be obtained as a quest reward after completing Betrothal Test, and can also be dropped by Sonicia Gogols.
Rafaga Armour is medium torso armour in and . It can be received as a quest reward and can be dropped by a number of enemies.

The Radiocarpea (Japanese: , Tekubi Kansetsubu) is a landmark in . It is located on the upper level of the Fallen Arm. It is first visited when Shulk, Fiora, Reyn and Sharla leave the 5th Pulse Zone and climb a path leading west. They are taken to the Hidden Machina Village shortly after climbing down.

Quadwing Treasures are rare materials in . They can be dropped by high level Quadwings in Satorl Marsh and Tephra Cave, or traded for in Frontier Village. According to their description, they are cursed items that makes the holder always lose at rock-paper-scissors. One is needed for Replica Monado 2.

This quest will expire if Brave Actions is completed first, or after the events at Mechonis Core. Protect the Capital! (Japanese: , Kōto no Anzen wo Mamore) is a Timed Quest in . It can be received from Lecrough during Brave Actions, and will expire if that quest is completed first. Both quests will expire after the events at Mechonis Core. Lecrough can be found at the bottom of the northern staircase in the Great Hall in Alcamoth.
Quality Horns are common materials in . They can be dropped by various Aries, Gogol, and the Magnis Ardun, but cannot be traded for.

Quality Frames are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from the Tranquil Morax, Fate Labolas, and various Mechon in Sword Valley and Galahad Fortress. Quality Frames are not available for trade.
Quality Plungers are rare material items in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are dropped by various large bipedal Mechon, or can be traded for.
Quality Plates are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by various Mechon and are not available through trading.
Quality Selua Cells are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are only dropped by certain Seluas in the Bionis' Interior.

Protective Torquidon (Japanese: , Chian no Tōkidon) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Tokilos family, and can be found at level 96 in Tephra Cave at the Heavenly Window landmark. It tends to show up once the hole in the ground at the Heavenly Window is approached. It can also respawn if the party Skip Travels to the Heavenly Window. It can drop the Tokilos King Egg needed for Replica Monado 5 and Colony 6 Reconstruction. It is immune to Break and Topple, but can be dazed by Dunban's Thunder art.

The Queen's Gut Fluid is a Key Item in . It is dropped by the Arachno Queen when the party tries to pass through Tephra Cave to go to Colony 6. It is used to dissolve the web which is blocking the passage from the Arachno Queen's Nest to Kneecap Hill.

The Radiant Pterix (Japanese: , Gokō no Puterusu) is a quest exclusive enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Pterix family, and can be found at level 86 above the Adulthood Emblem at the Sororal Statues in Satorl Marsh. The Radiant Pterix must be defeated to complete the quest The Imperial Ceremony.

Pterix Energy Eggs are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Pterix on the Fallen Arm, or traded for with Zarkort. According to their description, they are large eggs that make healing potions if blended in a special way. Two are needed for Lifespan of a Machina.

Rage (Japanese: , Reiji) is one of Reyn's arts in . Rage is an aura that reduces physical damage received by 25%, but also reduces the damage of Reyn's physical attacks by 25%. It gradually fills his Talent Gauge, and grants Reyn a Counter Spike effect which deals damage is equal to Reyn's Ether × 2. In , Nene has an identical version of this art called Hangry.

Radiocarpea Coast (Japanese: , Tekubi no Kaigan) is a location in . It is located on the lower level of the Fallen Arm. It is located at the south side of the arm's wrist, near the Giant Mechon Debris. Its name comes from the Radiocarpea landmark nearby on the upper level, and the radiocarpal joint which is a part of the human wrist.

Prosperous Zepar (Japanese: , Seiei no Zeparu) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Flamii family, and can be found at level 56 during the evening at Jifum Beach, on the Fallen Arm. It can be found between 17:00 and 19:00, just northeast of the mining station at Jifum Beach. It will land where the waves meet the sand at the northernmost part of the beach, and will not appear until the party walks right next to where it lands. It is much larger than the other birds nearby. It can drop the Pretty Flamii Legs needed for I Want to be a Homs!
is a Quadrupedal Enemy]] Quadrupedal Enemies are any of the creatures that walk on four legs. [B] = Boss [U] = Unique Monster [Q] = Quest Exclusive Enemy [S] = Story Exclusive Enemy
The Pure Water is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is needed for The Wilted Flower. It can be found at Zakt Spring, at the far opposite side of the Silver Wreckage.

Pulse Orlugas (Japanese: , Parusu Oruga) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Orluga family, and can be found at level 36 in Eryth Sea, three at Showdown Cliff and two within the Hode Refuge. They can drop the Orluga Slacks needed for Material Quest 3. There is a possibility that they are the untamed versions of Tocos Orlugas.

__FORCETOC__ Quarto Novas (Japanese: , Kuaruto Nova) are story exclusive enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Nebula family, and can be found at level 72 in Bionis' Interior only during the boss battle with Lorithia occurring into Bionis' heart. Although they do not respawn, several of them may be summoned during the course of the battle.

__FORCETOC__ Quinto Novas (Japanese: , Kuinto Nova) are story exclusive enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Nebula family, and can be found at level 72 in Bionis' Interior only during the boss battle with Lorithia occurring into Bionis' heart. Although they do not respawn, several of them may be summoned during the course of the battle.

The Proof of Courage is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is the objective of Challenge of the Sage, and must be retrieved from the Seahorse Islet in Makna Forest to prove the party's courage to the Nopon Sage.

Quest Enemies are Quest related enemies in . They must be defeated in order to complete a quest. Quest Enemies can be normal minor enemies as well as Unique Monsters. Defeating one or several precise enemies may be required in order to complete a "Monster Quest" type or a "Challenge" type quest. This request may also be ordered by a named NPC, during a Story Quest event, or during a Surprise Quest event. Some Quest Enemies are Quest Exclusive, they are one-of-a-kind and exclusively appear during a related Quest. They can only be defeated once per playthrough. A few of them are Story Exclusive Enemies or Bosses during Story Quest events, except one Boss during a Surprise Quest. There 201 Ques
Quality Lenses are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are not dropped by any enemies, but can be traded for with Shilx.
Pure-White Fangs are common materials in . They are only dropped by Shadow Vangs. No one has them available for trade.

Protection Masks are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be traded for with Cian when he is in Alcamoth. They are held by the Guard Entia for one battle but are not obtainable from drops nor by using Yoink!.
Quality Roes are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Satorl Tortas in Satorl Marsh.

Quality Maris Shells are rare materials in . They can only be traded for with Jiroque or Désirée. Quality Maris Shells are otherwise not available. According to their description, inverting them can make pots that lend a gourmet taste even to water.

Quality Insect Jaws are common materials in . They can be obtained from Royal Caterpiles on Bionis' Leg, Femuny Wisps in Tephra Cave, and various high-leveled Arachno and Pods. They are not available for trade.

Queen Cocoons are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be traded for with Zel Argentis, Peppino, and Ewan. (Note: Ewan only has the item available during the quest What is Courage?! while in Satorl Marsh.)
Quality Web Fibres are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from Ma'crish or Gorman.
Quality Units are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by M71 Flexible Units and the M71 Fire Support.
Quality Thrusters are rare materials designed for Xenoblade Chronicles. For unknown reasons they were cut from the game.
Quality Rhana Claws are rare materials in . They can only be obtained by trading with Rocco or Dulland.
Quiet Time (Japanese: , Odayakana Jikan) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located in the park in Colony 6, between Fiora and Riki at purple affinity.

Psycorruptor (known as Psy Seeker in the Japanese version) is a Class featured in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is one of two classes that can be leveled up from Enforcer and can be leveled up to Mastermind. The playable characters of this class include Mia, whereas each Celica's, Hope's and Irina's class is an Alternative Psycorruptor. Psycorruptor has 3 Skill slots.

Psycho Launchers are ranged weapons in . They are depicted as drone guns that fire multiple bursts of energy. Psycho Launchers are used primarily by the Blast Fencer and Galactic Knight Classes. Once the Galactic Knight class has been fully mastered, the weapons can be used regardless of class. Psycho Launchers are also the ranged weapons used by Hope, L, Murderess, and Neilnail.

Prospectors is a division within BLADE. This division is also known as Land Bank (Japanese: , Randobanku) in the Japanese version. They aim to maintain peoples' livelihoods by exploring Mira and securing resources. Their main duty is collecting minerals. Prospectors receive increased Division Points from mining with Data Probes and discovering new locations. Receiving division support from Prospectors grants Defense Support, which decreases the amount of damage sustained in battle.

Rage, Darkness of the Heart (怒り、心の闇, Anger, Darkness of the Heart) is an Event Track in and , composed and arranged by Manami Kiyota. It is track 11 of disc 2 from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack, and track eighteen of disc one from the Xenoblade Definitive Edition Original Soundtrack and the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This music is a dark, sad theme that is heard in the following cutscenes: *The entrance to the Weapon Development Lab blocked off to the party due to debris from the Mechon invasion * Metal Face and the Mechon retreat after their raid on Colony 9 * Otharon relates the tale of Gadolt's fate to Sharla and the rest of the party * Xord's final destruction in the
Quick Cannon is one of Irina's two Signature Arts in . It is a Ranged Art. Cross can learn it by completing Fathers and Sons.

Quick Evellos (Japanese: , Kuikku Sutorutto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Evello family, and can be found at level 11-16, near Roof Rock or on West Janpath Plain in Primordia during the day. Seven must be defeated while a party member is using the Diagonal Twins Dual Swords in order to complete That's In-Credible!.

raTEoREkiSImeAra is a track in , composed and arranged by Hiroyuki Sawano. It is track 13 of disc three from the XenobladeX Original Soundtrack. This track is composed of two themes which play at different times during the game. The first half is heard in the battle against Vita in the Lifehold Core. In the , the first half also plays during the battles against the Vita in Noctilum and Volitaris. The second half is heard during the cutscenes with the Telethia in Chapter 6 and The Nopon Heir, as well as battles with the Telethia. The uppercase letters in the title refer to Telethia. The lowercase letters in the title refer to the final boss, but this track is not otherwise associated with it.

Quest Exclusive Enemies are special enemies in . They are one-of-a-kind and exclusively appear during a related Quest. Most are also quest enemies, as they must be defeated to complete the quest in question. They can only be defeated once per playthrough like for the Story Exclusive Enemies. Quest Exclusive Enemies are essentially normal minor enemies with a normal target window frame when looking at them. They usually drop a silver Treasure Chest. Although some of them can respawn during the course of the related quest, they will not respawn once this quest is completed. However there are a few Unique Monsters with their related frames that are quest exclusive, as well as a few Story Exclus
The Ragrinar Canyon Path Shop is a shop in . It is located on the Bionis' Leg. It consists of a Homs merchant standing amidst a small group of Homs on the Ragrinar Canyon Path.

Prone Majors (Japanese: , Baiasu Mejā) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Prone troopers, and can be found at level 7-9 in Seaswept Base in Primordia. Two in particular can be found guarding FN Site 119.
Qing Long Glade (Japanese: , Seiryō no Hayashi) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Noctilum, northeast of FN Site 212.
Qing Long Glade BC (Japanese: , Seiryō no Hayashi BC) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Noctilum. The camp is operated primarily by the Pathfinders.
Puges (ベルデ, Berude, lit. Verde) are one of the Ganglion's human size robots in Xenoblade Chronicles X.

Prone Ruffians (Japanese: , Baiasu Rafian) are two story exclusive enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Prone troopers, and can be found at level 8 during Chapter 3. They assist Glennar during the boss battle event at the Seaswept Base in Primordia. One Ruffian carries an assault rifle that inflicts Physical damage, and uses the attacks Shockwave and Shrapnel. The other carries a beam rifle and uses the attack Debilitating Beam.
Prone Typhoons (Japanese: , Baiasu Taifūn) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Prone troopers, and can be found at level 8-10 at the Seaswept Base in Primordia.
Prone Hawks (Japanese: , Baiasu Hōku) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Prone troopers, and can be found at level 31-40 at Big Arch and FN Site 305 in Oblivia.

Raging Simius (Japanese: , Reiji Shimiusu, Rage Simius) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Simius and can be found at level 12-15 in Noctilum. Two must be defeated during Arms Testers Wanted.
Prone Purgers (Japanese: , Baiasu Pāji) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Prone and can be found at level 21-30 near Cliffside Camp or at Barbarich Desert in Oblivia.
Prone Warriors (Japanese: , Baiasu Woriā) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Prone and can be found at level 11-20 in Mesa Fortress or the Ruins on the Butte in Oblivia.
Prowler Mephites (Japanese: , Purourā Mepitesu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Mephite family, and can be found at level 11-15 on Aaroy Plain in Oblivia.

Quentin (Japanese: , Kuentin, English dub: ) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found near East Melville Street in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles during the day. He can be found near the Cathedral in the Residential District of New Los Angeles during the night.

Pure Ciniculas (Japanese: , Pyua Vasaruto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Cinicula family, and can be found at level 21-30 in the area southwest of Arendt Bridge, above the entrance to Molten Hollow in Primordia.
Raging Forfexes (Japanese: , Reiji Pagurusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Forfex family, and can be found at level 57-59 in NLA Waters.
